label: Futures Wheel
description: Expands one change into first, second, and third order impacts, helping trace indirect consequences, risks, opportunities, and affected stakeholders for discussion.

text_output_forms.primary_template: seed-change callout, three-order consequence ledger, discussion-priority bar chart, and uncertainty questions

required_blocks.title: Seed change
required_blocks.purpose: State one event or change point only.

required_blocks.title: Discussion priority, not likelihood
required_blocks.purpose: Rank two to five chains by attention needed on a 1–5 scale; values are for discussion, never probability.

text_output_forms.presentation_rule: Use branching causal language such as could or may. Do not turn the wheel into one linear story.

theory_mapping.source_notes: 思辨设计tools-3.pdf pages 15-16. External futures/design research tool.

model_constraints: Begin from one clear seed change.
Separate first-, second-, and third-order consequences.
Include indirect and unintended consequences, not only obvious benefits.
Do not describe impact chains as inevitable facts.
For text outputs, return the package text_blocks sequence, including a consequence table and a priority chart that is explicitly not a forecast.

reject_if: flat list with no consequence levels

ui.short_description: Expand one change into layered consequences.

recommendation.reason: Futures Wheel should first generate structured consequence chains, because the value is in distinguishing first-, second-, and third-order effects.
best_when: The input is a policy, product, platform change, technology event, or scenario seed.
The user needs indirect consequences rather than only the obvious outcome.
The next step is risk, opportunity, or priority discussion.

avoid: visual wheel without readable consequence labels

warnings: Prefer text unless the output will render a labelled diagram or feed a later visualization step.
